problem: Reach many customers at low cost without a quota-carrying field sales force.
title: Atlassian sells mostly through self-service with no direct sales team
context: Atlassian sold team software priced for volume and wanted to keep selling costs low.
decision_made: Let customers buy through the website with minimal friction and avoid a commissioned direct sales team, using partners for part of its sales.
action_taken: Executives said an enterprise customer could spend $10,000 and start with a team of 10 or 50 without talking to the company.
observed_outcome: Fortune reported in 2015 that Atlassian had been profitable for 12 years, which executives tied to the self-service model; sales and marketing was about 19 to 21 percent of revenue.
lessons: A product that sells itself can lower acquisition costs, though some support for large customers and partners still appears.
limitations: The no sales team claim is a simplification: there was a small sales function and about a quarter of revenue came through resellers. Profitability changed later (a 2022 CNBC piece said it was not actually profitable), and the F-1 filing was not read directly.

claims.claim_text: Atlassian relied on a self-service sales model, letting customers buy online without a sales call.
Fortune reported Atlassian had been profitable for 12 years, which executives attributed to the self-service model.
